decisions.reason: As a design-led extension of the core drainage range, the black-finish line fits current architectural preferences and is likely to stay despite only being briefly mentioned online at first.
A shower channel for seamless coverings is close to the firm's core offer, supports modern bathroom design trends, and its dedicated product page suggests clear commercial commitment.

Although more niche and technically demanding than standard drains, the pump-assisted shower solution expands the firm's barrier-free and difficult-installation offering, so it is more likely to be retained than withdrawn.
The tileable floor drain with grating is strongly aligned with the firm's established drainage business and its dedicated page indicates it is an intended part of the ongoing portfolio.
A stainless steel design grate is a low-risk adjacency to the existing range that reinforces the firm's design-and-engineering positioning and is therefore unlikely to be removed quickly.
